notes: Only TREND_CONFIRM has cohort-level power. BOUNCE (134) is aggregate-only; sub-slicing BOUNCE is under-powered.

Winner MAE profiles differ materially by Type. BOUNCE winners bleed ~2x deeper than TC winners — a uniform stop taxes BOUNCE more. Consistent with Kaminski & Lo (mean-reversion entry has deeper adverse excursion pre-win) and CLAUDE.md §7 hypothesis that BOUNCE differs from TC.

Every cohort with n>=30: expectancy is either monotone-to-no-stop OR the apparent optimum sits inside the no-stop bootstrap CI. Per guardrails sweep-discipline rule: NULL. Caveats stapled: fixed-% != trail; 30-bar truncation flatters no-stop; sizing not held constant. Panel window has NO sustained bear, so this does NOT refute the live stop — it only says a fixed-% stop shows no measurable expectancy edge on 2026-04..06 alone. H3 (behaviour bins add nothing over pattern) also passes for free: RSI/Gap/Vol/SMA_Dist tertiles inside TC show winner-MAE differences well below noise; no structure worth explaining with pattern labels.

Ranking mirrors auto_portfolio._pooled_cap: filter GOLD/PREMIUM, dedup by symbol per day, sort Quality asc / WinProb desc / R:R desc / Dist(<=25) desc / Vol desc, top-10=admitted. Known limits: does not model live open_syms, splits, or price-scale-mismatch skips - so admitted is the rankings intended order, not the executed set. Cap binds 42/43 days -> the natural experiment is dense.

Ranking works but is noisy. Directional at all horizons and 55-57 pct of days; only significant at 95 pct on episode-deduped ret_10d (+3.05pp CI [0.24, 5.86]) and on sign-test of median delta at 20d (p=0.044). May 2026 delta is negative (-3.79pp) - regime-dependent. Panel window is bull/mixed, no sustained bear.

The pooled ranking is doing exactly ONE thing: sorting by Quality tier (GOLD > PREMIUM). Everything below Quality is inert: WinProb is 99.8 pct NaN in the archive (calibration JSON is deliberately not deployed per section 7), R:R is a near-constant 2.5, Dist and Vol are the effective tiebreak but do not order forward returns within PREMIUM (rank buckets 01-10, 11-20, 21-50 within PREMIUM are non-monotone: 4.75, 5.67, 7.46). GOLD > PREMIUM is robust: stable in every month, holds within TREND_CONFIRM alone (+4.53pp at 20d, n=129 vs 1330), and by both modes. On avg 6-7 of the 10 daily admits fall into the PREMIUM sea where the sort is essentially random - this is the addressable gap.

verdict: PROMISING BUT NOT WALK-FORWARD-READY - do not promote, do not reopen H2 yet
notes: RSI (TREND_CONFIRM's own admission-time value, tightly banded 55-72 by the detector's existing gate) shows the largest, cleanest, most monotonic relationship to H5's hold-bucket split found so far: gt15d rate roughly triples from the bottom to top decile (21.3% to 66.4%), tracking win rate (36.1% to 51.4%), on n~140-160 per decile - well powered, and confirmed orthogonal to every feature the current ranking already uses (Quality, TC_Score, Vol). Unlike the Ridge model that sank the first H2 walk-forward attempt (coefficients reversed sign June vs training), a genuine within-April chronological split (first 5 trading days vs last 12) shows the RSI relationship REPLICATING, not reversing (rho 0.29 -> 0.45). However the pooled/decile numbers are 86% April by construction (1253/1459 episodes), and May (rho=-0.004, n=153) and June (rho=0.202, n=53) are both far weaker - plausibly because RSI's meaning is itself regime-dependent (a trend-strength proxy should behave differently across market regimes, exactly as BBG15/panic-throttle findings elsewhere in this project already assume), but equally plausibly just underpowered at n=50-150 to detect the same effect - the data cannot currently distinguish these. Gap% shows a similar-sized pooled spread (23.4pp) but is non-monotone (low 31%, mid 55%, high 50%) and degrades similarly out of April - a weaker candidate than RSI. Sector's 32.6pp spread across 8 cells is likely partly multiple-comparisons noise (8 categories, no correction applied) and is not being advanced as a candidate on its own. CONCLUSION: RSI is now the specific, sharpest candidate feature for H2's blocked walk-forward retry (sharper than raw ret_20d, which is what H2's original Ridge attempt targeted and failed on) - but it must wait for the same reopening trigger H2 already specifies (more frozen training days spanning more than one regime), because a single-regime-dominated in-sample finding is exactly the failure mode that sank the first attempt. No lever proposed, no ship decision - this narrows what the eventual retry should test first.
